messages:
Evan J: Kickoff - customers asking for a concise tenant-fencing playbook for private installs. Main asks: how to combine VLANs, k8s netpols, and KMS so tenants are strongly isolated? Quick opinions?
Maya R: For production we push a defense-in-depth model: physical/vlan segmentation + host hardening + k8s networkpolicy guardrails. VLANs reduce blast radius for L2 attacks.
Tao Z: Agree. Also recommend MAC/ARP inspection on the switch if available. L2 alone is brittle.
Olivia P: For KMS: deny cross-tenant decrypts by scoping keys to tenant aliases and using an allowlist of principals. Never give cluster-wide decrypt to node agents.
Hannah T: Compliance note: make sure key usage decisions are recorded with an immutable ID (e.g., kms_request_id) and exported to the customer's WORM storage for retention policies.
Evan J: What about operator workflows where SRE must access a tenant keystore during a response? How do we avoid standing privileges?
Tao Z: Short-lived checkout is best. Our pattern: an ephemeral role minted by an approval service (2-person approve) with TTL 10-15m, requiring an `incident_id` tag on the KMS call.
Maya R: We'll publish an example authorization flow. Also recommend MFA and just-in-time sudo for any host-level changes.
Olivia P: On audit: need to capture host info too (node ID, pod UID) and surface to SIEM. For private installs we doc how to forward to Splunk/ELK and include sample filter rules.
Evan J: Installer idea: add `rwi isolation-check` that runs a small battery and outputs pass/fail + details. Suggested checks?
Tao Z: My list:
- VLAN tag separation validated (probe from node A to B with expected VLAN)
- ARP probes across VLAN should be rejected
- netpol enforcement test (pod in tenant A cannot connect to pod in tenant B via TCP/UDP)
- KMS scope test (attempt decrypt with cross-tenant principal fails)
- Audit-forwarder handshake (TLS + certificate pinning)
- Host promiscuous mode disabled on bridges
Maya R: Make the netpol test automatable. Here's a minimal egress-block netpol we can ship as a quick test (adapted):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-egress-isolate
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      tenant: "${TENANT_ID}"
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: "10.0.${TENANT_CIDR}.0/24"
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
Olivia P: Note: netpols depend on CNI. Document the supported CNIs and noted limitations (e.g., calico vs. weave).
Hannah T: For incident play we should recommend a safe lockdown mode:
1) revoke active KMS grants for affected principals (async)
2) apply deny-all netpol overlay to tenant pods
3) quarantine nodes in the orchestration layer (cordon + network ACLs)
4) snapshot audit logs and persist to an external immutable store
Evan J: Caveat: revoking grants can be delayed. Recommend a short fanout: revoke -> apply temporary app read-only feature flag -> rotate ephemeral certs.
Tao Z: For air-gapped customers: support for HSM appliance (PKCS#11) and a KMS-proxy that runs in-datacenter. Proxy must require client certs and validate a local attestation token.
Maya R: Also add host-level eBPF L4 clamps as a recommended hardening: drop packets with inconsistent src MAC/IP combos, rate-limit ARP.
Olivia P: RBAC change process: require a GitHub PR with two approvers and a signed changelog entry for any permanent keystore RBAC grant. Enforce via policy engine if possible.
Hannah T: Compliance mapping: map each KMS action to a high-level control id so auditors can trace (e.g., KMS-AC-01: Key usage restricted by tenant tag).
sec-bot: Automation: isolation-check-runner started. Result: 4 checks passed, 1 flaky (ARP cross-VLAN probe). Created ticket: INTSEC-4821.
Evan J: Action items: Maya - write CNI-specific netpol guidance + limitations. Tao - spec `rwi isolation-check` tests and machine-readable output. Olivia - KMS scoping examples and proxy requirements. Hannah - compliance mappings and retention guidance. I'll stitch into a short playbook for customers.
Maya R: ETA for doc PR: 3 business days.
Tao Z: ETA for installer PR: end of week.
Olivia P: I'll prepare sample KMS policies and a BYOK proxy config template.
Hannah T: I'll prepare an auditor-facing appendix.
Evan J: Thanks all. Saving thread for follow-ups. Ping me if you need prioritization. :white_check_mark:
